note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `bandFromCompleteness` needs ALL 12 sections at 'complete' before it even checks the four mature drivers (nonDraftAdrs >= 5, fullyPopulatedQualityScenarios >= 3, risksWithMitigation >= 3, no medium-priority flag) — the second persona below deliberately meets every section's own (lower) completeness threshold without meeting the mature drivers, landing on 'ready' rather than 'mature'; the third persona strengthens exactly those three counts to cross into 'mature'.

personas.name: draft-early-stage-architecture

architecture.name: Payments Gateway Service
architecture.description: Central service that authorises, captures, and reconciles card and bank-transfer payments across all storefronts.

state.introduction: This document describes the architecture of the Payments Gateway Service, covering its context, structure, runtime behaviour, deployment, and quality attributes.

businessGoals.name: PCI DSS compliance
businessGoals.description: Achieve and maintain PCI DSS Level 1 compliance for all card-payment flows.

qualityGoals.name: Availability
qualityGoals.scenario: The service remains available for at least 99.95% of the time measured monthly, including during a single availability-zone failure.

qualityGoals.name: Security
qualityGoals.scenario: No card primary account numbers are stored outside the PCI-scoped vault at any point in the processing pipeline.

qualityGoals.name: Performance
qualityGoals.scenario: 95% of authorisation requests complete within 800ms under normal load.

stakeholders.name: Nadia Osei
stakeholders.concerns: Overall architectural integrity and compliance posture.

stakeholders.name: Marcus Webb
stakeholders.concerns: Feature delivery timelines and merchant experience.

constraintItems.name: PCI DSS scope isolation
constraintItems.description: Cardholder-data-environment services must run in a network-isolated PCI enclave.

state.businessContextDescription: The service integrates with storefronts, the finance/reconciliation system, and external acquiring banks and card schemes.
state.technicalContextDescription: The service exposes a REST API to internal storefronts and communicates with acquiring-bank APIs over mutually-authenticated TLS.

contextPartners.name: Storefront Checkout
contextPartners.interfaceDescription: Initiates payment authorisation and capture requests.

state.solutionStrategySummary: A PCI-isolated microservice fronted by a tokenising API gateway, using an event-driven ledger for reconciliation.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Memory safety and predictable low-latency performance for the authorisation hot path.

state.topLevelDecompositionSummary: Decomposed into an authorisation service, a tokenisation vault, and a reconciliation ledger.
state.buildingBlockOverview: Three top-level building blocks: Authorisation Service, Tokenisation Vault, and Reconciliation Ledger.

buildingBlocks.name: Authorisation Service
buildingBlocks.responsibility: Validates and routes authorisation requests to the acquiring bank.

buildingBlocks.name: Tokenisation Vault
buildingBlocks.responsibility: Stores and exchanges tokens for cardholder data within the PCI enclave.

buildingBlocks.name: Reconciliation Ledger
buildingBlocks.responsibility: Reconciles settled transactions against the acquiring bank statement.
buildingBlocks.interfaces: Nightly batch job, internal event bus.

state.runtimeOverview: A typical card-payment authorisation flow from checkout through to the acquiring bank and back.

runtimeScenarios.name: Card authorisation
runtimeScenarios.stepsSummary: Checkout calls Authorisation Service, which tokenises the card via the Vault and forwards the authorisation request to the Acquiring Bank Gateway, returning an approve/decline decision.

state.deploymentOverview: Deployed across two availability zones in the production PCI enclave.

deploymentNodes.responsibility: Hosts the Authorisation Service, Tokenisation Vault, and Reconciliation Ledger.

state.crosscuttingOverview: Shared concerns spanning all building blocks: audit logging and secrets management.

crosscuttingConcepts.name: Audit logging
crosscuttingConcepts.description: Every authorisation decision is written to an immutable, PCI-compliant audit log.

architecturalDecisions.title: Use Rust for the authorisation hot path
architecturalDecisions.context: Need predictable low-latency performance under PCI constraints.
architecturalDecisions.decision: Build the Authorisation Service in Rust with axum.
architecturalDecisions.consequences: Smaller talent pool but strong safety and performance guarantees.

architecturalDecisions.title: Tokenise cardholder data at ingress
architecturalDecisions.context: Minimise PCI DSS scope across the rest of the platform.
architecturalDecisions.decision: All cardholder data is tokenised at the API gateway before reaching downstream services.
architecturalDecisions.consequences: Downstream services never handle raw PANs, reducing audit scope.

architecturalDecisions.title: Event-driven reconciliation ledger
architecturalDecisions.context: Need an auditable, replayable reconciliation process.
architecturalDecisions.decision: Reconciliation is built as an event-sourced ledger rather than a mutable table.
architecturalDecisions.consequences: Higher storage cost but full replayability and audit trail.

state.qualityTreeSummary: Quality attributes prioritised: security, availability, then performance.

qualityScenarios.stimulus: Attempts to exfiltrate cardholder data from a downstream service.
qualityScenarios.response: No raw PAN is present outside the PCI enclave to exfiltrate.
qualityScenarios.measure: Verified by quarterly PCI DSS penetration test.

qualityScenarios.response: Traffic fails over to the healthy availability zone within 30 seconds.
qualityScenarios.measure: Monthly availability remains at or above 99.95%.

qualityScenarios.stimulus: Submits a payment authorisation request at peak load.
qualityScenarios.response: The request is authorised or declined.

riskItems.name: Acquiring bank API deprecation
riskItems.mitigation: Contractual 12-month deprecation notice; integration tested against the bank sandbox quarterly.

glossaryTerms.definition: Primary Account Number — the card number printed on a payment card.
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard.
Replacing a PAN with a non-sensitive surrogate value (token).
The bank that processes card payments on behalf of a merchant.
The transfer of funds from the acquiring bank to the merchant following a captured transaction.

state.additionalNotes: Ready for implementation; revisit after the first production quarter to assess for mature-band promotion.

personas.name: mature-all-drivers-met-no-flags
personas.description: The same payments-gateway architecture, further matured: 5 non-draft ADRs (was 3), and 3 risk items each carrying a mitigation, one of them technical debt (was 1 risk with mitigation), plus a documented coding convention — every section remains complete, all four mature drivers are now met (nonDraftAdrs >= 5, fullyPopulatedQualityScenarios >= 3, risksWithMitigation >= 3, no medium-priority flag), and the added convention/technical-debt entries also clear the two low-priority flags the previous revision carried: expect computedMaturity mature, finalMaturity mature (no override), and zero fired flags.

architecturalDecisions.title: Idempotency keys for authorisation requests
architecturalDecisions.context: Network retries must not double-authorise a payment.
architecturalDecisions.decision: Every authorisation request carries a client-generated idempotency key, deduplicated for 24 hours.
architecturalDecisions.consequences: Requires a low-latency deduplication store; adds minor complexity to the client SDK.

architecturalDecisions.title: Central audit log is append-only object storage
architecturalDecisions.context: Auditors require tamper-evident logs retained for 7 years.
architecturalDecisions.decision: Audit events are written to append-only, versioned object storage with object-lock retention.
architecturalDecisions.consequences: Slightly higher query latency for audit investigations, mitigated by a separate indexed read replica.
